photos.title_or_caption: Letter to the Editor by Walter Bookram: Representation and Public Rights
photos.transcription:
The Weekly Era (Raleigh, NC), c. 1873.
Letter to the Editor by Walter Bookram:
'Allow me space in your columns to address our citizens on matters of grave public concern and representation...
As a citizen who has long labored honestly among our people, I assert that true representation demands honesty, education, and fidelity to principle. We cannot afford to have our voices compromised or traded away by men who look only to immediate gain rather than the permanent elevation of our children and our communities. Let every man stand on his merits, let our rights be respected under the laws of this state and nation, and let us build schools, maintain our industry, and prove by our upright conduct that we are worthy of every privilege of free citizenship.'
(Signed) Walter Bookram.

photos.title_or_caption: Archival Feature: Elias Bookram - A Nanticoke Indian from Maryland in Granville County
photos.transcription:
Exhibition banner for Kianga Lucas's seminal research monograph 'Elias Bookram: A Nanticoke Indian from Maryland in Granville County' (Native American Roots, 2016).
Traces the descent of the Bookram family from the 1682 Nanticoke progenitor John Puckham of Somerset Co, MD to the Granville County indigenous community.

photos.title_or_caption: Historical Map: Nanticoke River, Chicacoan Town, and Broad Creek Reservation
photos.transcription: Detailed map showing the Nanticoke River flowing through Maryland and Delaware, locating the Chicacoan (Chicone) Reservation on the west bank of the Nanticoke River and the Broad Creek tract in Sussex County, Delaware.

photos.title_or_caption: Historical Map: Upper Eastern Shore Nanticoke Homeland
photos.transcription:
Map of the upper Delmarva Eastern Shore illustrating the indigenous homeland of the Nanticoke Tribe across Maryland and Delaware.
Source: Cohen, David, 'The One-Drop Rule in Reverse: The Nanticoke-Lenni Lenape, the Delaware Indians, and the New Jersey Indian Commission'.

photos.title_or_caption: Frank Speck Field Photograph: Nanticoke Community of Delaware (Plate 1, 1915)
photos.transcription:
Photographic plate from Frank G. Speck, 'The Nanticoke Community of Delaware', Museum of the American Indian, Heye Foundation, 1915.
Depicting members of the Nanticoke Indian community of Sussex County, Delaware, during Speck's field ethnography documenting remnant indigenous material culture, physical traits, and oral traditions.

photos.title_or_caption: Frank Speck Field Photograph: Nanticoke Community of Delaware (Plate 2, 1915)
photos.transcription:
Additional photographic plate from Frank G. Speck, 'The Nanticoke Community of Delaware', Museum of the American Indian, Heye Foundation, 1915.
Documenting Delaware Nanticoke family members and descendants in Sussex County.

photos.title_or_caption: Newspaper Advertisement: Walter Bookram, Practical Tanner (1875)
photos.transcription:
The Weekly Era (Raleigh, NC), 23 December 1875, Page 4.
'WALTER BOOKRAM, PRACTICAL TANNER.
The subscriber respectfully informs the public that he continues the TANNING BUSINESS in all its branches. Hides and skins tanned on the most reasonable terms, or taken on shares. Leather dressed in the best manner and finished with neatness and dispatch. Work warranted to give satisfaction.
Orders left at the office or sent by mail will meet with prompt attention.
(Signed) Walter Bookram.'

photos.title_or_caption: Granville County Deed Book Y, Page 63: Thomas Bonner to Elias Pookum (1814)

Granville County, North Carolina, Deed Book Y, Page 63.

Indenture between Thomas Bonner of Granville County and Elias Pookum (Bookram) of Granville County.

photos.title_or_caption: 1814 Granville County Tax List: Elias Puckham (Dutch District)

1814 Tax List of Granville County, North Carolina, Dutch District, taken by John Washington, Esq.
Entry:
Name: Elias Puckham
Acres of Land: 70
White Polls: 0
Black / Free Colored Polls: 1
Significance: Proves Elias Bookram was recorded under his ancestral Nanticoke surname 'Puckham' in Granville County official tax records in 1814.

photos.title_or_caption: Tribal Saga Excerpt: Chief George Puckham & 1742 Winnasoccum Treaty
photos.transcription:
Excerpt from 'We Are Still Here: The Tribal Saga of New Jersey\'s Nanticoke and Lenape Indians' by Rev. Dr. John R. Norwood.
Documents colonial Nanticoke leadership including Chief George Puckham, signatory to the 1742 Winnasoccum peace treaty following hostilities and land resistance in Somerset and Worcester counties on the Maryland Eastern Shore.
Traces the persistence and migration of Nanticoke Puckham families into Delaware, North Carolina, and New Jersey.

individuals.name: Elias Bookram
individuals.death_info: bet. 1850-1860 Dutchville, Granville County, North Carolina
individuals.notes: Progenitor of Granville County Bookram lineage. Nanticoke Indian born c. 1790 in Maryland; migrated to Granville Co, NC by 1814. Documented as Elias Pookum (1814 deed DB Y:63-64), Elias Puckham (1814 tax list), Elias Puckins (1820 census), Elias Puckram (1824 marriage bond), Elisha Buckram (1830 census), and Elias Bookram (1840, 1850 censuses). In 1850 census, birthplace explicitly recorded as Maryland. Lineal descendant of Chief George Puckham and 1682 progenitor John Puckham of Somerset Co, MD.
